summary:
May  


I didn’t want to write you, Sherry, until I felt better and wouldn’t bumtrip you. I know that one short letter did bumtrip you. You’re a very kind and sensi­ tive person. You deserve better friends than me. Or anyhow more cheerful ones. That telegram was outta sight! Wow! It was the only one we got, but even if God had sent one, plus a lot of lesser persons, yours would have been the best. I tried to phone you, but it has been hard to do anything right for me for a while, so I never got that all together (I kept thinking your number was LESSER S-F, but dialing that got me Cleveland again, as it always does. I then tried dialing LESSER F-S, which was the only other possibility I could imagine. Where did I go wrong?). 

Some money came in, so we got a used color TV and very fine stereo phones for the stereo. Now we have what the media calls a “home boredom cen­ ter” right in our living room, except that we only have an apartment, not a home. A “home” is what they will no doubt take me to one of these days when I am least expecting it; so I am expecting it, as a defensive tactic. We now, too, have a joint checking account; on our checks are pictures of rats, gophers, buzzards and other scenic wildlife. The best one shows a spider winding a bank vice president up in its web and smiling a lot. These cost extra, as the bank vice president prints them up himself. Or maybe the spider is wind­ ing me up, or maybe it’s the bank doing it. How many legs does a bank have? I forget...
